open_points.subject: execute_function_element / failed-element spool cleanup
open_points.text: On succeeded, each JSON output above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant concludes contract_violation with detail value_too_large, the SandboxResult's resources_used and no outputs; otherwise JSON outputs are published with put_value_bytes as StoredValues of the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), and files are published with spool_file under the run, node, map_index, the element's next attempt_number — the count of its NodeExecutions read with ExecutionsOfElement plus one, the number its record is then written under — the port and the list_index for a many port, a RefusedError from spool_file concluding resource_exhausted with the SandboxResult's resources_used, no outputs and no file of that attempt kept.
open_points.other_text: from cabinet_kernel.store import RefusedError, StoreInternalError, UnknownReferenceError, put_value_bytes, read_records, read_value_bytes, record_change, remove_run_spool, spool_file
open_points.question: Which passage must change: should a per-attempt/per-file spool-removal operation be imported, should spool_file provide atomic all-or-nothing publication, or should the requirement that no file of the failed attempt is kept be removed? The only imported removal operation removes the entire run spool, so after one file has been spooled and a later spool_file call raises RefusedError, the required attempt-local cleanup cannot be performed without also removing files belonging to other attempts.
